findings.body: Raise: Functional. A blocked PR opened by an earlier Forge release has neither a ready receipt nor the new `pull request published` event, so `published` is false even though the PR exists. `forge work` then publishes neither a worker question nor its answer to the PR record. A teammate's board cannot see the owner wait while the question blocks close. The same gap occurs when work continues in a checkout without either local marker.
findings.title: Questions on existing pull requests remain local

findings.body: Raise: Scale. This `git cat-file` call runs inside the read-round loop for every story on every board read. A client-sized board with roughly 100 stories and 10 cold-read rounds per story launches about 1,000 Git processes for `forge board --json`, and repeats that cost for the HTML page. The existing batched blob reader elsewhere in board.py shows these objects can be read without a process per round.
findings.title: Board launches Git once for every historical plan read

stop.reason: Owner chose narrow: fix the per-round git calls on board reads; questions on pull requests opened before this release stay local
